subject.title: [Feature]: Plugin API for aborting agent runs (api.runtime.agent.abort)

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-side run cancellation as `api.runtime.agent.abort({ runId })`, or should plugins use a narrower session-scoped cancellation seam instead?
rationale: The requested API is additive but grants plugins authority over active agent runs, so code inspection cannot decide the permanent plugin contract or security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design a scoped plugin cancellation API
options.body: Approve a narrow plugin-facing cancel/abort contract with explicit session/run ownership checks and then implement it with docs, SDK baseline, and focused gateway/runtime tests.

options.title: Use existing gateway/session abort only
options.body: Decline a new `api.runtime.agent.abort` method and instead document the supported gateway/session cancellation route or a separately approved plugin SDK subpath.

options.title: Defer plugin abort authority
options.body: Keep the issue open until a sponsoring plugin and maintainer-owned threat model make the required cancellation authority concrete.

recommendation.title: Design a scoped plugin cancellation API
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow plugin-facing cancel/abort contract with explicit session/run ownership checks and then implement it with docs, SDK baseline, and focused gateway/runtime tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has prior history on the plugin runtime contract and public SDK documentation surfaces where this product/security decision would land.
